items.title: Armand Hug Interview, 1976-02-13
items.q: The only ones that come to my mind is like Armstrong and Bonnie Berrigan.

ctx.x: Yeah, well, it's just that is there any value in trying to say that... trying to trace this to Emmett Hardy or what? I mean, it's obvious that Emmett Hardy was probably a great musician. I mean, you know, a lot of people testify to that. And that he probably had an influence on Bix's style. But what did Bix have... what did he contribute to the course of musical development? I guess you could say of jazz since the New Orleans style. Was his influence or contribution musically a harmonic in his use of harmonies?…

Right. Well, I can only say that as far as I'm concerned, he contributed. He contributed so much that it would be just hard to say what he did contribute, accepting that we know that all of these solos that he played were so original and so meaningful and so beautiful that really, if you analyze each one of his solos, they become almost... They become a masterpiece. Each one of them are a masterpiece. And you can almost make a tune or an arrangement out of each one of his solos. Yeah. Which is so amazing. I mean,…
Yeah, and you remember every solo. Pretty near. Very few of them. That's the most fantastic thing. And he remembers Trumbau by solos, too.
